Subject: SOC 2 Type II + interim continuity ask

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement asked me to collect standard evidence to complete EmberTech's vendor review before our enterprise kickoff. Two asks: 1) the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and 2) an interim continuity affirmation (a short attestation) that covers the period between the SOC report end date (2026-12-31) and now so our security team can close the control gap.

Can you confirm if Redwood can provide a one-page attestation that there have been no material control changes in scope or, if applicable, a short note describing any changes and mitigations? Our legal and InfoSec teams prefer a signed PDF.

Timeline: we'd like to have the documents by May 24 to keep the contract on track. Let me know if that is feasible.

Appreciate it — Liana

Attachments referenced: none

--

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Draft: interim continuity affirmation (v0.1)

Hannah / Karthik —

I put together a first-pass interim continuity affirmation based on the SOC scope and our change logs. Key points:
- Report: SOC 2 Type II, period ending 2026-12-31 (covering Security and Availability).
- Affirmation: As of May 17, 2027, Redwood Inference affirms that there have been no material changes to controls within the SOC 2 scope that would affect the report's assertions.
- Minor operational changes (routine KMS key rotation, small config tuning for autoscaling) were performed and are documented; none impact control objectives or scope.

I recommend we include a short appendix line listing the routine changes and point to our control change register (internal link) rather than a detailed narrative. Please review: if you approve I'll clean it up, add the signature block, and export as PDF for Liana.

Draft excerpt: "Redwood Inference affirms that, to the best of its knowledge, there have been no material changes to the controls within the scope of the SOC 2 Type II report (period ended 2026-12-31) through the date of this affirmation (May 17, 2027). Routine maintenance and scheduled cryptographic key rotations occurred as part of normal operations and did not affect the design or operating effectiveness of the controls tested in the report."

Questions for Hannah: do we want the compliance sig to be our Head of Security or Head of Compliance? Legal may prefer Compliance.

- Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Director, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Irene — this reads well. A couple small asks before we publish:
1) Add an extra line confirming KMS key rotation windows were covered by our monitoring alerts and no key material was exposed.
2) Add a one-sentence forward-looking statement: "This affirmation is limited to the period referenced and does not constitute a representation about future control performance."

I agree we should have the Head of Compliance sign. Hannah — once legal gives a quick thumbs I'll sign off and we can export PDF+DocuSign it.
